title: cost-optimization: autotune defaults for batching/caching, quant profiles, and unit-econ tooling
author: Anika Rao
description: Motivation: Reduce per-token serving cost by automating sensible defaults and providing tooling that recommends batching, caching and quantization profiles per model and workload. This change implements an autosuggest pipeline in the control plane that computes recommended batch_size/timeout and KV cache policies from traffic profiles, integrates quantization profile metadata into runtime selection, and surfaces unit-economics (tokens/cost) in the Console and Optimize APIs. Implementation: 1) control-plane autosuggest service that consumes sampling telemetry and persists recommended profiles; 2) runtime selection hooks to prefer recommended batch/cache/quant profiles with safe fallbacks; 3) unit-econ telemetry and a lightweight optimizer endpoint; 4) Console UI and API endpoints for viewing/applying recommendations. Checklist: - [x] design doc (Linear ENG-4123) - [x] unit tests for selection logic - [x] integration tests with perf-canary - [x] Console UI + API changes - [x] rollout canary and measured rollback strategy. Rollout and risk: Canary 5% on Dedicated and Hosted for 24h, monitor p95 latency, tail OOMs, and cost per 10k tokens; automatic rollback on >5% latency regression or increased error rate. Notes: This PR is intentionally conservative: recommendations are opt-in for private installs and default-suggest only for hosted; quantized runtime paths require model opt-in where available. See related perf-canary PRs for benchmarks.

release_notes: - Added control-plane autosuggest service to recommend batching/caching defaults and quantization profiles per workload. - Runtime now consults recommended profiles with safe fallbacks; 10% safety margin applied to batch_size. - Unit-economics telemetry and a Console panel to compare current vs recommended costs. - Schema migration to persist recommendation profiles.
